name: Battery Life Estimator
blurb: run time in days from average current and battery capacity
intro: Run time = usable capacity / (average load + self-discharge). Usable capacity is the rated mAh times a derating for cut-off voltage, temperature and ageing; self-discharge is turned into an equivalent current from the chemistry's typical monthly loss. The result is capped by the cell's shelf life.

inputs.label: Capacity per cell
inputs.help: 0 = typical for the chosen battery (Li-ion/LiPo and LiFePO4 need yours).

inputs.label: Cells in parallel
inputs.help: Series cells add voltage, not mAh: count only parallel strings.

inputs.label: Average current
inputs.help: From the sleep current profiler, or measured (10u = 10 µA).

inputs.label: Peak current
inputs.help: Largest burst, e.g. a radio transmit. 0 = no check.

inputs.label: Usable fraction
inputs.help: Derating for cut-off voltage, cold and ageing; 70 … 90 % is usual.

examples.title: BLE sensor on a CR2032 at 10 µA average, 15 mA TX bursts
Tracker on a 2000 mAh LiPo at 1.2 mA

usage: Choose the battery chemistry (or custom with self-discharge in %/month and shelf life in years), the capacity per cell in mAh (0 = typical), cells in parallel, the average current in A, the peak current in A (0 = skip) and the usable fraction in %. It returns the run time in hours, days, months and years, the usable capacity, the self-discharge as an equivalent current, whether shelf life or self-discharge limits it, and warnings when the average or peak current is more than the cell is rated for.
sources: Battery University BU-802b 'What does elevated self-discharge do?' (self-discharge by chemistry)
Energizer CR2032 / CR2450, E91 alkaline and L91 lithium product datasheets (capacity, drain limits); Tadiran / Saft ER14505 datasheets (Li-SOCl2)
